questions.stem: Which pattern should direct the nurse's immediate teaching and protective actions?
questions.scenario: A client 12 hours after transsphenoidal surgery has clear nasal drainage with a salty taste and keeps asking whether it is safe to blow the nose.
questions.additionalInfo: The client also wants to sip through a straw and cough hard because the throat feels dry.

options.text: Possible CSF leak requiring avoidance of maneuvers that increase nasal or intracranial pressure
Routine postoperative mucus that should clear after nose blowing
Expected sinus drainage with no special precautions
Dehydration only, best managed with straw use and fluids

questions.rationale: Clear salty drainage after transsphenoidal surgery should be read as a possible CSF leak. The nurse should connect the symptom to pressure-avoidance teaching and escalation, not routine sinus care.

distractorRationales.b: "Routine postoperative mucus that should clear after nose blowing" misses the bedside risk. The cue "A client 12 hours after transsphenoidal surgery has clear nasal drainage with a salty taste and keeps asking" points to circulation or perfusion. Teaching items should reinforce the specific medication, symptom, or safety rule rather than inventing a new emergency.
distractorRationales.c: This distractor shifts care toward false reassurance instead of patient teaching and medication-safety reinforcement. The stem cue "The nurse should connect the symptom to pressure-avoidance teaching and escalation, not routine sinus care" makes circulation or perfusion the active safety concern.
distractorRationales.d: "Dehydration only, best managed with straw use and fluids" commits to a competing cause before checking the dangerous pattern. The cue "A client 12 hours after transsphenoidal surgery has clear nasal drainage with a salty taste and keeps asking" raises concern for circulation or perfusion, so patient teaching and medication-safety reinforcement is needed before diagnostic reassurance.

questions.takeaway: Salty clear drainage after transsphenoidal surgery is a leak clue until proven otherwise.
questions.speedCue: The surgery type plus the salty drainage should make the answer immediate.
